# makeclient

> Create and host an OAuth Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) at a URL you use
> directly as a `client_id` — no registration, no backend. Built by Authlete to
> exercise CIMD-capable OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authorization servers.

A CIMD client is an OAuth client whose identity is a JSON document served at an
HTTPS URL that *is* the `client_id`. The authorization server fetches that URL
to read the client's metadata and keys, so there is no registration step. This
replaces Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) for stateless and agent use cases
(e.g. MCP, the Personal Agent Protocol).

## Create a CIMD client

Public (PKCE) client — config encoded in the URL, stateless:

```
curl -s https://makeclient.dev/api/clients \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"redirect_uris":["https://app.example/cb"]}'
# → { "client_id": "https://makeclient.dev/c/<cfg>/client-metadata.json" }
```

Confidential (`private_key_jwt`) client — mints an ES256 keypair; the public key
goes in the document, the private key is returned and never stored:

```
curl -s https://makeclient.dev/api/clients \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"token_endpoint_auth_method":"private_key_jwt"}'
# → { "client_id": "https://makeclient.dev/s/<id>/client-metadata.json",
#     "private_key": { ...JWK... } }
```

`GET` the `client_id` URL to see the document. Any RFC 7591 client-metadata
field may be set in the POST body to override the defaults.

## API

- `POST https://makeclient.dev/api/clients` — create a client; returns
  `client_id` (plus `private_key` for `private_key_jwt`).
- `GET https://makeclient.dev/oauth/client-metadata.json` — the all-defaults
  public client document.
- OpenAPI: https://makeclient.dev/openapi.json
